_note: Clinical Intelligence is decision support with a doctor's signature: the clinical inbox, review and sign, structured consultations, triage on ratified protocols, result acknowledgement, Home Guidance and PROMs. Every protocol in packages/catalog/protocols.json is a draft today, so every triage and guidance call is refused in practice until the board ratifies one. Wave 2 contract; Wave 5 build.

refusals.statement: Nothing is triaged without a ratified protocol.
refusals.why: Software does not triage until the board has ratified the rules it triages by.

refusals.statement: No model output lowers a priority the rules set.
refusals.why: §15D: generative AI may explain a priority; it may not lower one.

refusals.statement: No output tells a patient they have a condition.
refusals.why: Findings are "consistent with", for a clinician to confirm (§5.3).
A note is signed by a doctor's own action.

refusals.statement: A result is not complete until a clinician acknowledges it.
refusals.why: An unacknowledged result is a loop nobody closed.

refusals.statement: Only a doctor on the panel reads the inbox.
refusals.why: The inbox is other people's care.

routes.summary: A doctor signs a review, under a named protocol version.

refusals.statement: A review is signed under a named protocol version.
refusals.why: Every recommendation cites the version it was made under.

refusals.statement: That protocol version is not ratified.

refusals.why: The open conflict in the build plan: the board ratifies first.

refusals.statement: Nothing lowers a priority the rules set.
refusals.why: A red flag is never AI-gated.

withdrawn.why: It returned the rules' reason codes outside the Passport gateway, and triage.completed@1 carried them to Access, Care and Safety. A reason code names the discriminator that fired — which symptom, which red flag — and so is clinical content: it is written to the record and read there by a clinician.
